exploration.title: Gravity Drop Lab
exploration.subject: Physics
exploration.summary: Compare how object mass and local gravity affect a vacuum drop.
exploration.question: What changes a vacuum drop: object mass or local gravity?
exploration.explanation: Mass is the amount of matter in an object; weight is the gravitational force on it. In a vacuum at one location, objects released together from the same height have the same acceleration regardless of mass. Changing local gravity changes acceleration and weight, while mass stays fixed. This near-surface model uses constant local gravity.

experiments.title: Compare masses fairly
experiments.instruction: Keep Earth gravity and a 20 m release height fixed. Predict which lands first, then compare 1 kg with 10 kg.
experiments.observe: Both land in 2.02 s, while their weights are 9.81 N and 98.1 N. Explain why weight changes but vacuum acceleration does not.

experiments.title: Compare worlds
experiments.instruction: Keep mass at 5 kg and the release height at 20 m. Predict which drop takes longer, then compare Earth with the Moon.
experiments.observe: Earth takes 2.02 s and the Moon takes 4.97 s. Explain why weaker local gravity changes the fall while mass stays fixed.

exploration.misconception: More weight does not produce more free-fall acceleration when gravity is the only force: the added gravitational force and added inertia scale together. Air resistance can change real-world results.
